messages:
kevin: FYI found a class of websocket clients that choke on our new control frames (resume, meta-heartbeat). they close with 1002 on unexpected frame type. proposal: implement a coalescing shim that turns new control frames into application-level keepalive events (single text frame) for opt-in tenants.

nina: can you sketch the on-wire change? is it lossy for clients that *do* understand new frames?

kevin: lossy only when shim is enabled. pseudo-rules:
```
if headers['X-RW-Compat-SOCKET']=='coalesce=v1':
  server: when about-to-send(control_frame): buffer -> emit text({"type":"rw_ctrl","payload":base64(ctrl)})
  client: legacy clients receive plain text keepalive, they ignore unknown json -> survive
```
This preserves sequence semantics (we serialize control frames in order).

charlie: big concern = memory: buffering control frames while waiting to emit a coalesced text blob could increase p99 memory on the edge. what's expected rate?

kevin: control frames are low-volume (<1% of traffic) and small, but bursts exist (reconnect storms). we'll cap buffer to 16 frames and emit sooner. fallback: drop excess control frames and emit a `rw_ctrl_overflow=true` flag so operators know.

vijay: what about ordering w.r.t. streaming tokens? if we mix control->data, we must keep strict ordering otherwise clients see weird interleaving.

kevin: ordering preserved: we treat control frames as part of the same append-only stream and only coalesce contiguous control frames; when a data frame arrives, we flush pending control blob first.

maria: billing / metering note: the shim will add wrapper bytes around control frames. we must not charge customers for shim overhead. can we tag coalesced text frames with `X-RW-Shim: coalesce-v1` and make meter ignore wrapper bytes?

vijay: adding a shim tag header is fine for HTTP but not for raw websocket frames. we can inject an out-of-band pilot header on websocket session creation (session-metadata) like `rw.shim=coalesce-v1` that the billing service reads.

nina: deployment model? edge only? sidecar? both?

kevin: plan:
- implement coalescer in edge proxy (hosted) behind tenant opt-in header
- provide a sidecar library for Dedicated/Private for customers who want to enable locally
- add a lightweight wasm module option for edge teams that prefer sandboxing

charlie: perf: how much extra CPU? rough estimate?

kevin: initial bench: +2-6% CPU at 95th when coalescing enabled on canary load. We need to run sustained canary.

ops-bot: canary build queued: branch compat/socket-coalesce-v1 -> canary-682. logs will be available in ~15m.

maria: testing checklist:
- fuzz old clients (close on unknown frames) against coalescer
- replay 48h production socket traffic against shim in read-only mode and compare session traces
- ensure no token delta in billing tests
- latency histogram and p50/p95 comparisons

vijay: monitoring ideas: metrics `compat.socket.coalesce.enabled`, `compat.socket.coalesce.buffer_overflow`, `compat.socket.coalesce.cpu_pct`. add an alert for buffer_overflow > 0.1% over 10m.

charlie: security: ensure we don't accidentally expose serialized control payloads to the app layer. must be base64 and signed with session key so apps can't inject fake control frames.

kevin: good point. we'll HMAC the coalesced blob with session MAC and validate on decode. customers who later migrate to new frames can be offered a migration tool to unpack historical logs.

nina: product constraint: this shim is a migration aid, not a new API. deprecation policy: mark as temporary, review after 3 months of tenant opt-ins. document clearly in changelog and console.

maria: console: add toggle under "Connections -> Compat" with audit entry and tenant consent checkbox. alex (cc) will need to wire UI.

kevin: action items: kevin -> prototype wasm & edge impl, charlie -> mem/CPU bench, vijay -> billing tagging plan, maria -> tests & console spec, nina -> short RFC and deprecation wording.

deploy-bot: canary deployed (id: canary-682) at 3951236825 by kevin

ops-bot: alert rule added: `compat.socket.coalesce.buffer_overflow > 0.1% for 10m` -> page to eng-infra

nina: thanks all. i'll open rfc/compat-socket-coalesce with the tickets linked and add owners. any objections to proceeding with staged canary?

charlie: +1 from infra side, watch memory closely.

vijay: +1 for billing safety checks.

maria: +1 from QA.

kevin: proceeding. will update thread with canary metrics in 2 hours.
